title: How the power grid works
examples: Why do we need transformers when sending electricity?
What is the difference between the power station and my house?
How does electricity get from the power station to my street?

explain.say: Today we will learn about the power grid. It moves electricity to your home safely.

items: Pylons/Transmission Lines: Power travels long distances

draw.text: Power Grid: From Station to Home

explain.say: Power stations create electricity using different sources. Some use burning fuel, others use water.
Transformers change the voltage level. Step-up transformers increase the voltage for long travel.
Pylons carry the electricity on high-tension wires. These lines must carry the power over long distances.
Step-down transformers lower the voltage before it reaches neighbourhoods. This makes it safe for use.
In your home, the final low voltage is safe for your lights and appliances to use.

faq.q: Why is electricity sent at high voltage?
faq.a: It is sent at high voltage because it reduces the current needed for the same amount of power. This means less energy is lost over long distances.
asks: Why do we need to boost the voltage?
What is the point of high voltage transmission?

faq.q: What happens if the voltage is too low?
faq.a: If the voltage is too low, the power delivered to your home will be weak. Your lights might flicker or appliances might not work correctly.
asks: Will my TV work if the voltage is low?
What causes weak electricity at home?

faq.q: Do all power stations use the same energy source?
faq.a: No, power stations use many sources. Some burn fossil fuels, while others use renewable sources like wind or water.
asks: Can power stations use solar power?
Are all power stations powered by coal?

faq.q: What is the job of the pylons?
faq.a: The pylons support the high-tension wires carrying electricity. They keep the wires safely suspended between supports.
asks: What are the big metal towers for?
Do pylons carry all the electricity?

faq.q: How does the voltage get safe enough for my TV?
faq.a: Step-down transformers reduce the high voltage from the pylons to a safe, usable level for local areas and homes.
asks: Why do we need transformers near my street?
What lowers the voltage before it enters my house?

facts: Electricity generation happens at power stations.
Step-up transformers increase voltage for transmission.
Pylons carry electricity over long distances.
Step-down transformers reduce voltage for local use.

quiz.say: Electricity needs to be boosted before travelling far.
quiz.why: The step-up transformer increases voltage so less energy is lost over distance.

wrong.0: A pylon only supports the wires; it does not change the voltage level.
wrong.1: The power station creates the electricity, but the transformer changes the voltage.
wrong.3: This lowers the voltage, which is needed near the end, not at the start.

quiz.say: What changes the voltage before it enters a neighbourhood?
quiz.why: The step-down transformer lowers the very high voltage to a safer level for local distribution.

wrong.1: This increases voltage, which is the opposite of what is needed here.
wrong.2: Pylons only support the wires; they do not perform voltage changes.
wrong.3: The power station generates the initial power, not specifically for lowering the voltage.

quiz.say: If electricity travels from a power station to a city, what is the general process?

options.show: Only pylons are needed for the whole process.
options.say: Only pylons are needed for the whole process.

options.show: Electricity travels directly from station to home.
options.say: Electricity travels directly from station to home.

quiz.why: The power must be increased for travel and then decreased before it reaches homes.

wrong.0: Pylons only support the wires; transformers manage the voltage.
wrong.2: You must lower the voltage at some point for household safety.
wrong.3: This would result in extremely high, unsafe voltages at home.
